Data Communication Systems

Overview:
Interconnected devices exchange packets across shared infrastructure to reach distant endpoints reliably.

Addressing:
Each node on the network is assigned a unique numeric label so that outgoing traffic knows where to go next.

Congestion:
When too many packets arrive at once, queues build up and some transmissions must be dropped or delayed.

Security:
Encryption scrambles the contents of a message so eavesdroppers cannot read it in transit.

Bandwidth:
The maximum throughput of a link is measured in bits per second and limits how much data can move at once.
